content.title: Suns vs. Spurs: Prediction, How to Watch for Free (3/19/26)
content.text: The Phoenix Suns (39–30) face the San Antonio Spurs (51–18) tonight at Frost Bank Center in San Antonio. The Suns enter on a three-game losing streak despite continued high-level play from Devin Booker. On Tuesday, they fell to the Minnesota Timberwolves, 116–104, with Booker pouring in 34 points. He’s averaging 37.0 PPG over his last four outings and 31.2 this month. But the supporting cast struggled to keep pace. Jalen Green — who had been on a surge of his own, averaging 27.5 points per game over his previous six contests — managed just nine points, shooting 3-of-17 from the field. Collin Gillespie’s difficulties also continued, as he finished with 12 points on 4-of-13 shooting. As a result, Phoenix’s recent momentum has stalled. The Suns sit seventh in the Western Conference, currently positioned for a play-in tournament spot, but just 2.5 games behind the Houston Rockets and Denver Nuggets for the final automatic playoff berths. They now face a San Antonio team that has won three straight and eight of its last 10 games. The Spurs are locked in a two-team battle with the Oklahoma City Thunder for the top seed in the West, with OKC riding an 11-game winning streak of its own. San Antonio routed the Sacramento Kings, 132–104, on Tuesday in a game that allowed starters to rest in the second half and extend minutes to the bench. Thirteen Spurs players saw the floor, with Keldon Johnson scoring 18 points in just 20 minutes. Victor Wembanyama also tallied 18 points while playing only 22 minutes. Phoenix leads the season series 2–1, though the Spurs won the most recent meeting in emphatic fashion, cruising to a 121–94 victory in February. San Antonio’s balanced scoring and current form give it the edge tonight. Still, Phoenix has a path to an upset if Booker stays hot and Green rebounds offensively. Prediction: San Antonio Spurs 121, Phoenix Suns 115 Injury Report Phoenix Suns Haywood Highsmith — GTD (Knee) Royce O’Neale — Out (Knee) Grayson Allen — GTD (Knee) Dillon Brooks — Out (Hand) Mark Williams — Out (Foot) San Antonio Spurs David Jones Garcia — OFS (Ankle) How to Watch Suns vs. Spurs Tip-off for tonight’s Suns-Spurs game is set for 8:00 PM Eastern / 7:00 PM Central / 5:00 PM Mountain at the Frost Bank Center in San Antonio. The game airs live locally on Arizona’s Family Sports and FanDuel Sports Network Southwest. Out-of-market viewers can stream the matchup on NBA League Pass for free on Amazon Prime Video with a 7-day free trial here.
